questions.q: What is net investment?
options: Sum of all the investments in a country
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gross investment - depreciation.

Key Points

• A company's net investment is the sum of its expenditures on capital assets less the cost of depreciating those assets.

• This gives an idea of the actual spending on durable products utilized by the company in its operations, such as buildings, machinery, and software.

Additional Information

• Depreciation: It means a fall in the value of an asset because of usage or with efflux of time or due to obsolescence or accident.

• Appreciation: It means an increase in the value of an asset over time. This the opposite of depreciation. It is an upward adjustment of the value of an asset held on a company's accounting book.

• Deceleration: It is the rate at which an asset's value in the market goes down.

• Gross investment: It is the total amount spent on goods in order to produce other goods and services.

• Net investment: It is the amount of increase in productive stock.

•

Capital investment is the money used by a business to purchase fixed assets, such as land, machinery, or buildings. The money may be in the form of cash, assets, or loans. Without capital investment, businesses may have a hard time getting off the ground.

• The time frame was nearly 756 to 773 AD.

• The temple is the largest of the rock-cut Hindu temples at the Ellora Caves.

• It is considered one of the most remarkable cave temples in the world because of its size, architecture and sculptural treatment.

• According to the same inscription, he defeated the invincible Karnata-Bala of the Badami Chalukyas.

• In addition, he defeated the kings of Lata (Gujarat), Malwa, Tanka, Kalinga and Sheshas (Nagas) in central India.

questions.q: Microbes like Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are used for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is nitrogen cycling.

Key Points

•
Nitrogen Cycle-

• Nitrogen is an essential constituent of protein and is a basic building block of all living tissue. It constitutes nearly 16% by weight of all the proteins that is, converted to ammonia, nitrites or nitrates before it can be taken up by plants.

• Nitrogen fixation on earth is accomplished in three different ways:

a) By microorganisms (bacteria and blue-green algae)

b) By man using industrial processes (fertilizer factories) and

c) To a limited extent by atmospheric phenomena such as thunder and lighting

• Certain microorganisms are capable of fixing atmospheric nitrogen into ammonium ions. These include free-living nitrifying bacteria (e.g. aerobic Azotobacter and anaerobic Clostridium) and symbiotic nitrifying bacteria living in association with leguminous plants and symbiotic bacteria living in non-leguminous root nodule plants (e.g. Rhizobium) as well as blue-green algae (e.g. Anabaena, Spirulina).

• Ammonium ions can be directly taken up as a source of nitrogen by some plants, or are oxidized to nitrites or nitrates by two groups of specialised bacteria: Nitrosomonas bacteria promote the transformation of ammonia into nitrite. Nitrite is then further transformed into nitrate by the bacteria Nitrobacter.

• The nitrates synthesised by bacteria in the soil are taken up by plants and converted into amino acids, which are the building blocks of proteins. These then go through higher trophic levels of the ecosystem. During excretion and upon the death of all organisms nitrogen is returned to the soil in the form of ammonia.

• Certain quantities of soil nitrates, being highly soluble in water, are lost to the system by being transported away by surface run-off or groundwater. In the soil as well as oceans there are special denitrifying bacteria (e.g. Pseudomonas), which convert the nitrates/nitrites to elemental nitrogen. This nitrogen escapes into the atmosphere, thus completing the cycle.

• The periodic thunderstorms convert the gaseous nitrogen in the atmosphere to ammonia and nitrates which eventually reach the earth’s surface through precipitation and then into the soil to be utilized by plants.

Additional Information

• Carbon Cycle

• The carbon cycle involves several processes, including photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, and combustion. Plants absorb carbon dioxide (CO₂) during photosynthesis, while animals release CO₂ through respiration.

• Carbon is stored in various reservoirs, including the atmosphere (as CO₂), oceans (as dissolved CO₂ and organic carbon), soil (as organic matter), and living organisms. These reservoirs play a crucial role in regulating global climate.

• Human activities, such as fossil fuel combustion and deforestation, significantly alter the carbon cycle by increasing atmospheric CO₂ levels, contributing to global warming and climate change.​

• Water Cycle-

• The hydrologic cycle is the continuous circulation of water in the Earth-atmosphere system which is driven by solar energy. Water on our planet is stored in major reservoirs like atmosphere, oceans, lakes, rivers, soils, glaciers, snowfields, and groundwater. Water moves from one reservoir to another by the processes of evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, deposition, runoff, infiltration, and groundwater flow.

• Water as an important ecological factor determines the structure and function of the ecosystem. Cycling of all other nutrients is also dependent upon water as it provides their transportation during the various steps. It acts as a solvent medium for their uptake of nutrients by organisms.

• Sulphur Cycle-

• The sulphur reservoir is in the soil and sediments where it is locked in organic (coal, oil and peat) and inorganic deposits (pyrite rock and sulphur rock) in the form of sulphates, sulphides and organic sulphur.

• It is released by weathering of rocks, erosional runoff and decomposition of organic matter and is carried to terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems in a salt solution.

• The sulphur cycle is mostly sedimentary except two of its compounds hydrogen sulphide (H2S) and sulphur dioxide (SO2) add a gaseous component to its normal sedimentary cycle.

• Sulphur enters the atmosphere from several sources like volcanic eruptions, combustion of fossil fuels, from the surface of the ocean and from gases released by decomposition. Atmospheric hydrogen sulphide also gets oxidised into sulphur dioxide.

• Atmospheric sulphur dioxide is carried back to the earth after being dissolved in rainwater as weak sulphuric acid.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that 'there shall be a Vice President of India'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 63.

Key Points

• Article 63

• Article 63 of the Indian Constitution states that "There shall be a vice president of India."

• The vice president acts as president in the absence of the president due to death, resignation, impeachment, or other situations.

• The vice president of India is also ex officio chairperson of the Rajya Sabha. When a bill is introduced in Rajya Sabha, the vice president decides whether it is a financial bill or not.

• If he is of the opinion, a bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha is a money bill, he would refer the case to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha for deciding it.

Additional Information

• Article 61

• The process for the impeachment of the President is outlined in Article 61 of the Indian Constitution.

• Either House of Parliament may file the impeachment accusations.

• The President must be notified 14 days in advance, and these allegations must be signed by one-fourth of the House members who framed them.

• The other House, which is tasked with conducting an investigation into the allegations, receives the impeachment resolution when it has been approved by a two-thirds majority of the entire membership of that House.

• The President has the right to show up and be represented during such an investigation.

• The President is removed from office as of the date the resolution is passed if the other House concurs with the accusations and approves the impeachment resolution with a two-thirds majority of its members.

• Impeachment is a quasi-judicial process in Parliament as a result.

• In this context, it is important to keep in mind two things:

• nominated members of either House of Parliament may take part in the impeachment of the President even though they did not cast a ballot in his election;

• and elected members of state legislative assemblies and the union territories of Delhi and Puducherry may not, even though they cast a ballot in the President's election.

• Article 65

• Article 65 deals with the Vice-President acting as President or discharging the functions of the President in the event of a vacancy.

• ​Article 62

• Article 62 of the Indian Constitution deals with the time frame for holding an election to fill a vacancy in the office of the President.

• Oxygen (O) has an oxidation number of -2.

• The overall charge of the molecule is 0.

• So, we can set up the equation:

• 2(+1) + 2(x) + 7(-2) = 0

• Simplifying:

• 2x = 12

questions.q: Which digits should come in place * and $,respectively, if the number 72864*$ is divisible by both 8 and 5?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a number to be divisible by 5, its last digit ($) must be 0 or 5.

For a number to be divisible by 8, it must be an even number, so $ must be 0.

The last three digits (4*0) must be divisible by 8.

Checking the given options, if * = 4, the number 440 is divisible by 8 (440 ÷ 8 = 55).

∴ The correct answer is 4 and 0.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number = 72864*$

The number is perfectly divisible by both 8 and 5.

Concept Used:

Divisibility by 5: The unit digit must be 0 or 5.

Divisibility by 8: The number formed by the last three digits must be divisible by 8.

Calculation:

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 5, the unit digit $ can be 0 or 5.

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 8, it must be an even number. Hence, $ cannot be 5.

⇒ ∴ $ = 0

⇒ The last three digits form the number 4*0.

⇒ Now, we check the given options for *.

⇒ If * = 4, the number formed is 440. Since 440 ÷ 8 = 55, it is completely divisible by 8.

⇒ If * = 2, the number formed is 420. Since 420 ÷ 8 = 52.5, it is not completely divisible by 8.

⇒ ∴ The missing digits are * = 4 and $ = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 4 and 0.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 3 & 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is completely divisible by 3 or 9, respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 4 & 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd places and the sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.q: The incomes of P, Q and R are in the ratio 10 : 12 : 9 and their expenditures are in the ratio 12 : 15 : 8. If Q saves 25% of his income, then what is the ratio of the savings of P, Q and R?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Q saves 25% of his income, which means Q's expenditure is 75% of his income.

Ratio of Q's Expenditure to Income = 75% = 3 / 4 ⇒ 15y / 12x = 3 / 4.

This gives y / x = (3 / 4) × (12 / 15) = 3 / 5 ⇒ x / y = 5 / 3. Let x = 5 and y = 3.

Savings = Income − Expenditure ⇒ P = (10×5 − 12×3), Q = (12×5 − 15×3), R = (9×5 − 8×3).

Savings Ratio = (50 − 36) : (60 − 45) : (45 − 24) = 14 : 15 : 21.

∴ The correct answer is 14 : 15 : 21.

Alternate Method

Given:

Income ratio of P, Q, R = 10 : 12 : 9

Expenditure ratio of P, Q, R = 12 : 15 : 8

Savings of Q = 25% of Q's income



Formula Used:

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Calculations:

⇒ Let the incomes of P, Q, and R be 10x, 12x, and 9x respectively.

⇒ Let the expenditures of P, Q, and R be 12y, 15y, and 8y respectively.

⇒ Q's saving = Q's income − Q's expenditure

⇒ Q's saving = 12x − 15y

⇒ It is given that Q saves 25% of his income:

⇒ 12x − 15y = 25% of 12x

⇒ 12x − 15y = (25 / 100) × 12x

⇒ 12x − 15y = 3x

⇒ 9x = 15y ⇒ y = (9 / 15)x = (3 / 5)x

⇒ Now substituting y = 3x / 5 to find savings of all three:

⇒ Saving of P = 10x − 12y = 10x − 12 × (3x / 5) = 10x − 36x / 5 = 14x / 5

⇒ Saving of Q = 12x − 15y = 12x − 15 × (3x / 5) = 12x − 9x = 3x = 15x / 5

⇒ Saving of R = 9x − 8y = 9x − 8 × (3x / 5) = 9x − 24x / 5 = 21x / 5

⇒ Ratio of savings = 14x / 5 : 15x / 5 : 21x / 5

⇒ Ratio = 14 : 15 : 21

∴ The correct answer is 14 : 15 : 21.

Additional Information

Income, Expenditure & Savings

The fundamental relation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. If income and expenditure are given in separate ratios, using independent variables for each helps to find the relationship between them via any given connecting condition.

Ratio Multipliers

A ratio a : b implies actual values are ax and bx where x is a common multiplier. When two different groups of quantities are in ratios, they require two different variables (e.g., x and y).

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting percentages to fractions (like 25% = 1/4) simplifies calculation involving equations. Thus, 25% savings implies 75% (or 3/4) of income is expenditure.

⇒ Since we already have AB = FD and the included angle ∠A = ∠D, the other pair of sides forming these equal angles must also be equivalent to satisfy the SAS criteria.

⇒ Therefore, the side AC of ΔABC must be exactly equal to the side DE of ΔDEF.

⇒ AC = DE

∴ The correct answer is AC = DE.

Additional Information

SSS (Side-Side-Side) Congruence

If all three sides of one triangle are structurally equal to the corresponding three sides of another triangle, then the triangles are fully congruent.

ASA (Angle-Side-Angle) Congruence

If two angles and the included side between them in one triangle are equal to the corresponding parts of another triangle, then the triangles are congruent.

AAS (Angle-Angle-Side) Congruence

If two adjacent angles and a non-included side of one triangle are equal to the corresponding consecutive angles and side of another triangle, they are congruent.

RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side) Congruence

If in two right-angled triangles, the hypotenuse and one standard side of one triangle are identical to the hypotenuse and corresponding side of the other, they are congruent.

questions.q: A payment of ₹120 is made with ₹10, ₹5 and ₹2 coins. A total of 25 coins are used. Which of the following is the number of ₹10 coins used in the payment?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume all 25 coins are of the lowest denomination (₹2). Base value = 25 × 2 = ₹50.

Extra amount to be matched to reach ₹120 = 120 − 50 = ₹70.

Each ₹10 coin adds ₹8 extra, and each ₹5 coin adds ₹3 extra compared to a ₹2 coin. Let their numbers be x and y.

This forms the equation: 8x + 3y = 70.

Checking the options for x: If x = 8, then 8(8) + 3y = 70 ⇒ 64 + 3y = 70 ⇒ 3y = 6 ⇒ y = 2 (Valid integer).

∴ The correct answer is 8 coins.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total number of coins used = 25

Total payment made = ₹120

Let the number of ₹10 coins be x, ₹5 coins be y, and ₹2 coins be z.

Equations:

⇒ x + y + z = 25 ... (i)

⇒ 10x + 5y + 2z = 120 ... (ii)



Calculations:

⇒ Multiply equation (i) by 2:

⇒ 2x + 2y + 2z = 50 ... (iii)

⇒ Subtract equation (iii) from equation (ii) to eliminate z:

⇒ (10x + 5y + 2z) − (2x + 2y + 2z) = 120 − 50

⇒ 8x + 3y = 70

⇒ Since x and y must be positive integers, let's test the given options for the value of x:

⇒ Option 1: x = 6 ⇒ 48 + 3y = 70 ⇒ 3y = 22 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 2: x = 4 ⇒ 32 + 3y = 70 ⇒ 3y = 38 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 3: x = 10 ⇒ 80 + 3y = 70 ⇒ 3y = −10 (Not possible as count cannot be negative)

⇒ Option 4: x = 8 ⇒ 64 + 3y = 70 ⇒ 3y = 6 ⇒ y = 2 (Valid integer)

⇒ Substitute x = 8 and y = 2 in equation (i) to find z:

⇒ 8 + 2 + z = 25 ⇒ z = 15.

⇒ Cross-verifying the total value: (8 × 10) + (2 × 5) + (15 × 2) = 80 + 10 + 30 = ₹120.

∴ The correct answer is 8 coins.

Additional Information

Diophantine Equations

A linear equation of the form ax + by = c where only integer solutions are expected. When counting physical objects like coins, the variables must strictly be non-negative integers.

Elimination Method

A structured algebraic technique to solve simultaneous equations by multiplying with constants to equalize the coefficients of one variable, and then subtracting equations to eliminate it.

Average Denomination Rule

The overall average value of each coin provides a good estimation point. Here, Average = Total Amount ÷ Total Coins = 120 ÷ 25 = ₹4.8, which helps logic check your final ratio.

∴ The correct answer is 12320 cm³.

Height of cylinder (h) = 20 cm

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 1760 cm²

Formula Used:

LSA = 2πrh

Volume = πr²h

⇒ r = 14 cm

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

Shortcut Trick

Multiply inside the root by the conjugate of the denominator: (1 + sin θ).

The denominator becomes 1 − sin² θ = cos² θ.

The numerator becomes (1 + sin θ)².

Taking the square root gives (1 + sin θ) ÷ cos θ.

Splitting the terms gives (1 ÷ cos θ) + (sin θ ÷ cos θ) = sec θ + tan θ.

∴ The correct answer is sec θ + tan θ.

sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ

tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ

Rationalise the denominator by multiplying the numerator and the denominator by (1 + sin θ):

⇒ √[ { (1 + sin θ) × (1 + sin θ) } ÷ { (1 − sin θ) × (1 + sin θ) } ]

⇒ √[ (1 + sin θ)² ÷ (1 − sin² θ) ]

⇒ √[ (1 + sin θ)² ÷ cos² θ ]

Removing the square root:

⇒ (1 + sin θ) ÷ cos θ

Distributing the denominator:

⇒ (1 ÷ cos θ) + (sin θ ÷ cos θ)

⇒ sec θ + tan θ

∴ The correct answer is sec θ + tan θ.

Additional Information

Standard Trigonometric Results

√[(1 − sin θ) ÷ (1 + sin θ)] = sec θ − tan θ

Cosine Equivalent Results

Pythagorean Identities

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 | sec² θ − tan² θ = 1 | cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1

Rationalisation Strategy

For square roots of trigonometric fractions (like 1 ± sin θ), multiplying by the conjugate of the denominator easily converts the expression into a perfect square, allowing direct simplification.

questions.q: M and N walk along a circular track. They start at 5:00 a.m. from the same point in the opposite directions. M and N walk at a speed of 5 rounds per hour and 2 rounds per hour, respectively. How many times will they cross each other before 6.30 a.m. on the same day?

Shortcut Trick

When bodies move in opposite directions on a circular track, they cross each other at a frequency equal to the sum of their speeds in rounds per unit time.

Relative speed = 5 + 2 = 7 rounds per hour.

This means they cross each other 7 times every hour.

Total time from 5:00 a.m. to 6:30 a.m. = 1.5 hours.

Total crossings = 7 × 1.5 = 10.5 crossings.

∴ The correct answer is 10 times.

Time interval = 5:00 a.m. to 6:30 a.m. = 1.5 hours

⇒ Hence, they cross each other 7 times in 1 hour.

⇒ In 1.5 hours, relative laps completed = 7 × 1.5 = 10.5 laps.

⇒ Since a crossing occurs for every fully completed relative lap, we take the integer value.

⇒ Number of times they completely cross each other = 10

∴ The correct answer is 10 times.

Meetings in Opposite Directions

When moving in opposite directions, the frequency of meetings per unit time is the sum of their individual speeds (rounds per unit time): S₁ + S₂.

Meetings in Same Direction

When moving in the same direction, the frequency of meetings per unit time is the difference of their individual speeds: |S₁ − S₂|.

Meeting at the Starting Point

Regardless of the direction, the time taken to meet for the first time at the starting point is the LCM of the individual times taken by each person to complete one full round.

questions.q: The measures of the three angles of a triangle are in the ratio 17 : 13 : 15. Find the positive difference between the greatest and the smallest of these three angles.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total parts of the angles = 17 + 13 + 15 = 45 parts.

We know the sum of the interior angles of a triangle is always 180°.

45 parts = 180° ⇒ 1 part = 4°.

Difference between greatest (17) and smallest (13) angle parts = 17 − 13 = 4 parts.

Difference in degrees = 4 parts × 4° = 16°.

∴ The correct answer is 16°.

Alternate Method

Now, calculate the values of the greatest and smallest angles:

questions.q: A certain sum of money becomes seven times itself when invested at a certain rate of simple interest, in 14 years. How much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will it take to become 18 times itself at the same rate?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct formula for Simple Interest multiples: T₂ = [(n₂ − 1) ÷ (n₁ − 1)] × T₁

Given n₁ = 7, T₁ = 14 years, and n₂ = 18.

T₂ = [(18 − 1) ÷ (7 − 1)] × 14 = (17 ÷ 6) × 14

T₂ = (17 × 7) ÷ 3 = 119 ÷ 3 = 39.666... ≈ 39.67

∴ The correct answer is 39.67 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial sum = P

Amount after 14 years (A₁) = 7P

Target Amount (A₂) = 18P

⇒ 6P = (P × R × 14) ÷ 100

⇒ R = (6P × 100) ÷ (14 × P) = 600 ÷ 14 = 300 ÷ 7 %

Case 2:

⇒ Interest (I₂) = 18P − P = 17P

⇒ 17P = (P × R × T₂) ÷ 100

∴ The correct answer is 39.67 years.

Additional Information

Direct Relation for Simple Interest Multiples

If a sum becomes 'n' times itself in 'T' years at simple interest, the rate of interest is given by R = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ T.

Simple vs Compound Interest Concept

In Simple Interest, the interest remains constant for each year. In Compound Interest, the interest gets added to the principal and acts as the new principal for the next period.

Rule of 72

A general estimation trick used in finance: to find the approximate number of years it takes to double your money at a given compound interest rate 'R', divide 72 by R.
